page.overview:
What is MissingNo.?

MissingNo. (Japanese: けつばん Ketsuban) is a name shared by several glitch Pokémon in Pokémon Red, Blue, and also Yellow. The name is most commonly used to refer to a /-type glitch Pokémon whose sprite consists of corrupted data or a / in Pokémon Yellow. It is arguably the most well-known glitch in the overall game series.

In the earliest Pokémon video games, the programmers had to use variables to refer to different Pokémon by number. Due to the 8-bit memory, variable sizes must be powers of two. The smallest variable they were able to use was the size of one byte—that is, capable of holding any value from 0 to 255 with zero counting as a slot. (The next smallest size could only hold 0 to 127, which would not have been enough for all 151 Pokémon.) Because there are only 151 legitimate Pokémon in Generation I, this left 105 slots unoccupied. 37% of these are occupied by empty slots named MissingNo., 53% are Trainers (this is the reason why "wild" trainers are sometimes found on the coastline of Cinnabar Island), and the rest are other glitch Pokémon.

Unlike most glitch Pokémon, whose names consist of data cobbled together from random locations, MissingNo.'s name is clearly a deliberately-added abbreviation of "missing number". This is because "MissingNo." was added as a name for the empty slots to avoid the game crashing if a glitch Pokémon was encountered.

The MissingNo. most commonly encountered during glitches is a Normal/Bird-type Pokémon, whose sprite is a backwards letter "L"-shaped chunk of glitched pixels. Bird is a beta type that was deleted from the final game (presumably Flying); it functions identically to Normal. The sprite results from the game treating non-graphical data as an image. This form of MissingNo. almost always knows Sky Attack and Water Gun; of particular note is the fact that it knows two Water Gun moves. The fossil and Ghost sprites of MissingNo. have the same moveset as the most recently viewed Pokémon. The player can encounter it in all Generation I games, though in Yellow, MissingNo. was encountered in a different way. MissingNo.'s stats will change depending on the player character's last party Pokémon. It should be noted that Missingno. often appears in levels beyond 100 - the maximum of the core series (though it can still easily be defeated).
